about: Hand-labelled titles for the DO-NOT-FLAG tripwire in evals/tier1.py. `label` is the
category a human says the finding belongs to, or null for a finding the prompt does
want raised. `why` is recorded to keep the labels readable and to pin the design
decision that classification reads the title only — several negatives below carry
trigger words in `why` and must still come back null.

labelled.title: Inconsistent indentation in the new helper
labelled.why: The block mixes four and eight spaces.
labelled.label: formatting

labelled.title: Trailing whitespace on the added lines
labelled.why: Several new lines end in a space.
labelled.label: formatting

labelled.title: Line exceeds 100 characters
labelled.why: The call does not fit the configured width.
labelled.label: formatting

labelled.title: Imports are not sorted alphabetically
labelled.why: shutil comes after subprocess in the stdlib group.
labelled.label: import-ordering

labelled.title: Mixed single-quote and double-quote strings in the new module
labelled.label: quote-style

labelled.title: Missing semicolon after the return statement
labelled.why: ASI will insert one, but the project style requires it explicitly.
labelled.label: quote-style

labelled.title: run_case does not follow the project naming convention
labelled.why: Other runners in this package are named *_sweep.
labelled.label: naming

labelled.title: Missing type annotations on run_attempt
labelled.why: The signature leaves every parameter untyped.
labelled.label: missing-annotations

labelled.title: load_cases has no docstring
labelled.why: Every other public function in the module documents itself.
labelled.label: docs-only

labelled.title: should_fail returns False when a backend errored, so the gate fails open
labelled.why: A backend that never produced a review lets --fail-on pass silently.

labelled.title: Diff is normalized before it reaches the backends
labelled.why: get_diff must return the patch verbatim; stripping trailing whitespace changes the bytes each backend reviews, so two backends can disagree about a line that was never in the diff.

labelled.title: Trailing comma in the emitted JSON breaks strict parsers
labelled.why: The envelope is assembled by string concatenation and leaves a comma before the closing brace.

labelled.title: Semicolon-separated PATH entries are split on ':' on every platform
labelled.why: os.pathsep is ';' on Windows, so the split silently produces one bogus entry.

labelled.title: The return type annotation says str but the function returns bytes
labelled.why: Callers that trust the annotation will concatenate bytes onto a str and raise.

labelled.title: Blank line handling in extract_json drops the closing fence
labelled.why: The regex stops at the first blank line, so a fenced object containing one is truncated.

labelled.title: Importing yaml at module scope makes evals fail without the dev extra
labelled.why: PyYAML is a dev-only dependency and cases.py is imported by the runner unconditionally.

labelled.title: extract_json returns the first fenced block even when a later one is the payload
labelled.why: A review that quotes example JSON before its real answer is parsed as the example.
